title: kbmon --status and kb_monitor_status say an absent or timed-out panel's own reason
goal: kbmon --status PANEL and the kb_monitor_status tool print the reason an absent or timed-out panel gives (an absent coord store names the store, an unreachable server names the refusal), as --once and --json do, not only the state word

run:
import os,subprocess as s,sys,tempfile
d=tempfile.mkdtemp();st=os.path.join(d,'none.sqlite');kf=os.path.join(d,'k');open(kf,'w').write('planted'+'x'*20);os.chmod(kf,0o600)
env=dict(os.environ,COLUMNS='400')
a=s.run([sys.executable,'_tools/kbmon.py','--status','coord','--store',st],capture_output=True,text=True,env=env,timeout=120).stdout
b=s.run([sys.executable,'_tools/kbmon.py','--status','coord','--url','http://127.0.0.1:9','--key-file',kf],capture_output=True,text=True,env=env,timeout=120).stdout
print(a.strip()[:300]);print(b.strip()[:300])
sys.exit(0 if os.path.basename(d) in a and 'refused' in b.lower() else 1)
